content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 75+ values).
- Model underreacts to sharp downward moves; fails to anticipate sharp drops in price after high peaks.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds prices too high after peaks, ignoring recent downward momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model lacks downward adjustment mechanism.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent low prices — often fails to recognize when prices are trending down.
- Overshoot correction needed after spikes: reduce forecast by 5–10% of peak value in subsequent days.
- Apply downward bias adjustment if history shows 3+ consecutive days of falling prices.
- Avoid overfitting to recent high values — model should not assume continuation of recent peaks unless confirmed by momentum indicators.
